TIL that in 2012, a group of juvenile gorillas were seen successfully disarming poachers' traps and snares, as well as warning nearby humans away from it.

TIL in the 18th century many prominent voices were concerned by an 'epidemic' affecting young people whereby they were spending too much time reading books. It was diagnosed as 'a dangerous disease' called ‘reading rage, reading fever, reading mania or reading lust.'

TIL that in 2012, trading firm Knight Capital lost over $460 million in just 45 minutes after a software deployment error caused its computers to execute millions of unintended stock trades. Its systems had generated 97 warning emails before the market even opened.

TIL Leopold II of Belgium had an illegitimate son born with a deformed hand. This led to a cartoon depicting Leopold holding the child, surrounded by the corpses of Congolese who had their hands cut off, with a caption reading "Vengeance from on high".

TIL that Henry Flagler transformed a tiny Florida settlement known as Fort Dallas into the city of Miami almost overnight in 1896. When residents offered to name the new city after him, he declined the honor and asked that it be called Miami instead.

TIL that all tequila is actually mezcal. Mezcal is a distilled spirit made from any type of agave plant. Tequila can only be made from blue agave in Jalisco. Under the NOM-070 Mezcal standard, the Jalisco state is excluded from geographic origin so no tequila can be legally called mezcal.

TIL that unborn sand tiger sharks develop teeth and eyes early to hunt and eat their own siblings in the womb. Females have two uteri, and the first pup to hatch in each one kills and consumes all the others until only two survive to be born
TIL in 2025, a genetically modified pig kidney kept a living human patient off dialysis for a record 271 days before being removed and successfully replaced with a human donor kidney
TIL that Chinese men in Hong Kong could legally take concubines according to the legal code of the Qing Dynasty until 1971.
TIL in the aftermath of the failed Bay of Pigs invasion, the US and Cuba agreed to settle for $53 million(about $591 million today) of baby food and medicine in exchange for prisoners.
